request: Evaluate bare OpenCode again, then evaluate the next five installed tools with OpenCode.

selection_rule.primary_order: ascending raw provider tokens in the latest accepted compatible GPT-5.6 Sol/high panel
selection_rule.secondary_metric: weighted tokens = fresh input + 0.1 * cached input + 6 * output
exclusions: products already evaluated with OpenCode: TokenJuice, Serena, Snip, Cartog, Headroom
products without a pinned native or host-agnostic OpenCode integration surface
selection_rule.canonical_profile_policy: Use the latest valid full-product profile rather than historical partial or neutral ablations, then map only product-authored native or host-agnostic surfaces to OpenCode.

fresh_baseline.execution_order: baseline first; treatments may start only after all three accepted baseline sessions are retained

selected.opencode_surface: host-agnostic MCP server, official initialize instructions, and warm index
selected.compatibility_evidence: /opt/data/tool-candidates/codescope-release-v0.8.12/README.md states any MCP-compatible agent may use the product

selected.opencode_surface: official OpenCode rules, project skill, native plugin, MCP, and warm vault
selected.compatibility_evidence: official `install --agent opencode --hook` surface in the pinned source

selected.opencode_surface: official OpenCode project skill, AGENTS guidance, native pre-tool plugin, and warm graph
selected.compatibility_evidence: official `graphify install --platform opencode --project` surface in the pinned wheel
official `rtk init --global --opencode` surface in the pinned binary/source

selected.opencode_surface: official local OpenCode installer, MCP server, model-runtime CLI, and warm live index
selected.compatibility_evidence: official `codegraph install --target opencode` integration in the pinned source

explicit_exclusion.reason: The pinned Token Savior product has Codex-specific hooks and generic MCP/guidance but no OpenCode integration surface. Mapping or inventing its hooks would be an evaluator-authored ablation rather than installing the product with OpenCode.

preflight_corrections.initial_failure: OpenCode debug-info probe could not enter the generated project path because project-scoped plugins were prepared but the project was not mounted into the preflight container.
preflight_corrections.fix: The preflight controller now mounts and uses the fixture repository only for profiles declaring preflight_requires_project; SwarmVault and Graphify declare it.
preflight_corrections.verification: A fresh direct container prepare-only run passed exact compiled/generated artifact checks, OpenCode plugin debug proof, MCP initialize plus tools/list, and warmup.

preflight_corrections.initial_failure: The pinned Graphify wheel exposes a graphify-mcp executable on its private PATH although this OpenCode profile does not activate the MCP server; the command-visibility gate initially treated that same-product executable as an undeclared treatment.
preflight_corrections.fix: Allowlisted the exact graphify-mcp command term while leaving the MCP server unconfigured and absent from the profile component/surface declaration.
preflight_corrections.verification: Runtime contract requires graphify-mcp to be an allowlisted same-product command and requires no mcp_server in the active profile. Full provider-free retry required.

preflight_corrections.initial_failure: The RTK plugin was installed and byte-verified in the isolated OpenCode home, but the adapter was told to use the unmounted fixture path as its debug-info working directory.
preflight_corrections.fix: Removed the unnecessary project-directory override for the global RTK plugin profile; the debug probe now runs from the mounted isolated OpenCode home.
preflight_corrections.verification: Runtime contract requires the RTK profile to omit OPENCODE_EVALUATION_DIRECTORY while retaining the exact installed plugin hash. Provider-free retry required.
